chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about wudu (ablution), and he said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform wudu (ablution) with one mudd of water, and perform ghusl with one sāʿ.”

key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before acts of worship
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.صَاعٍ: a sāʿ, a larger measured quantity of water
key_terms.مُدٍّ: a mudd, a measured quantity of water

ai.seo_question: How much water did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم use for wudu (ablution) and ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding the amount of water used for wudu (ablution) and ghusl. It serves as a juridical and practical precedent for moderation and sufficiency in ritual purification.
